title: The Sixteenth Recipe
premise: Orsen Whitlock can bake feelings into bread — grief makes loaves dense, joy makes them rise impossibly — a gift inherited from the founders of Millbrook, whose Sixteen Recipes built the town itself. When a group chat called The Sixteenth begins predicting disasters before they happen, Orsen realizes someone is weaponizing the lost sixteenth recipe, the one that bakes the future. With prom as the deadline and the town's founding tradition about to be erased by the council that corrupted it, Orsen and four friends must recover the true recipe and choose between exposing the truth that will shatter Millbrook or protecting the people they love. In the end, Orsen bakes the sixteenth recipe one final time — not to predict the future, but to return choice to the town — and lets the tradition die so something honest can rise in its place.
about_author: Oscar Eriksen is the pen name of a former bakery apprentice from the Pacific Northwest who spent three years writing this novel between 4 a.m. shifts. They write stories about small towns, inherited magic, and the weight of family recipes.

chapters.title: Proofing
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. On the last stretch before graduation, Orsen bakes a loaf for a grieving classmate and watches it come out black-crusted, confirming their secret gift still works. Establishes the bakery, the countdown mentality, and the ache of wanting to leave Millbrook. Emotional beat: restless suffocation.

chapters.title: The Group Chat Nobody Made
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A chat appears on five phones at once — Orsen, best friend Devi, crush Junia, rival Theo, and quiet Marisol — predicting a water tower failure two days early. It happens exactly as written. Beat: cold dread disguised as a joke.

chapters.title: Second Prediction
chapters.summary: Devi's POV. The chat predicts a teacher's resignation with a specific sentence she'll say aloud; it comes true word for word. Devi, a skeptic, starts a spreadsheet of predictions versus outcomes. Beat: rationality cracking under evidence.

chapters.title: Flour and Ash
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen researches the town's founding: sixteen recipes baked into the charter, fifteen preserved in the historical society, the sixteenth 'lost.' Grandma Whitlock goes pale when asked and forbids further digging. Beat: first taste of family secrecy.

chapters.title: Theo Knows Something
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo, councilman's son, admits his father has been receiving predictions for months — and acting on them, quietly profiting. Theo joined the chat hoping to catch him. Beat: reluctant alliance across old grudges.

chapters.title: The Fifteenth Recipe
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The five break into the historical society and read the surviving recipes — each one a civic ritual (the harvest bread, the mourning loaf). Marisol, an archivist's daughter, finds a ledger page torn where the sixteenth should be. Beat: wonder curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Prediction: Fire
chapters.summary: Junia's POV. The chat predicts the bakery will burn on Thursday. Junia, who has been avoiding Orsen since a middle-school betrayal, warns them anyway. The fire is small, contained — but clearly set. Beat: guilt and tenderness entangled.

chapters.title: What the Council Keeps
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen confronts Theo's father, who reveals the sixteenth recipe was never lost — the council has used it for decades to 'steer' the town, baking futures that benefit themselves. He offers Orsen a place in it. Beat: temptation wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Loyalty Test
chapters.summary: Devi's POV. The chat predicts Devi will betray the group. Devi hides the prediction, then catches herself editing what she tells the others. Beat: paranoia — is the prediction forcing her, or is she?

chapters.title: Grandma's Confession
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Grandma Whitlock admits she was the last Baker of Record; she walked away after the council forced her to bake a future that destroyed a family — Junia's family, it turns out. Beat: inheritance revealed as wound.

chapters.title: Prom Is the Deadline
chapters.summary: Junia's POV. The council announces the Founders' Bake at prom, where a new Baker of Record will be sworn in — Theo's father's handpicked candidate. The chat goes silent for the first time. Beat: the trap closing.

chapters.title: Stolen Pages
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol recovers the torn ledger half from the council archive, revealing the sixteenth recipe is incomplete without a Baker's genuine feeling — which is why the council's futures keep souring. Beat: hope with a mechanism.

chapters.title: The Betrayal
chapters.summary: Devi's POV. Devi's hidden prediction comes true: cornered by the council, she gives up the group's plan. She confesses immediately, but trust fractures. Beat: loyalty vs. truth made personal.

chapters.title: Baking Bad Futures
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo finds his father's private oven room — decades of baked futures, each one a small cruelty dressed as prosperity. Theo photographs everything. Beat: disillusionment turned to resolve.

chapters.title: Reconciliation in Dough
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen bakes forgiveness bread for Devi — not magic, just honest work — and the group rebuilds trust by telling each other every secret they've kept, including Orsen's feelings for Junia. Beat: bruised but mended.

chapters.title: The Night Before Prom
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. The group plans to swap the council's ceremonial bake with a true sixteenth recipe at prom. The chat returns with one final prediction: 'One of you will not walk out.' Beat: fear sharpened into commitment.

chapters.title: Founders' Bake
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. At prom, the council's candidate begins the corrupted ritual. Orsen interrupts, claiming Baker's right by blood, and begins baking the true recipe in front of the whole town. Beat: public defiance.

chapters.title: What the Bread Shows
chapters.summary: Junia's POV. As the true sixteenth recipe rises, everyone who eats it sees the futures the council stole from them — including Junia seeing the life her family lost. The crowd turns on the council. Beat: cathartic reckoning.

chapters.title: The Price of Truth
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo's father, exposed, tries to destroy the oven room and nearly takes Marisol with it — fulfilling the final prediction. Theo pulls her out; his father is arrested. Beat: justice outside the law, paid in family.

chapters.title: Letting the Recipe Die
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Offered the Baker of Record title, Orsen refuses and bakes the sixteenth recipe one last time as plain bread — no futures in it — then burns the original pages. Choice returned, prophecy ended. Beat: renunciation as triumph.

chapters.title: Graduation
chapters.summary: Devi's POV. Graduation day: the town debates its future openly for the first time, the bakery reopens under Grandma and Orsen together, and the group chat sends one last message — 'Thank you' — then deletes itself forever. Beat: earned lightness.

chapters.title: The First Recipe
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, epilogue. Summer's start: Orsen and Junia bake the founding harvest bread for a town that no longer needs magic to hold together. Orsen finally counts days forward instead of down. Beat: beginning instead of sentence served.
